newsitem.title: USA: U.S corporate debt issuance at year-end standstill.
newsitem.headline: U.S corporate debt issuance at year-end standstill.

text.p: Corporate debt new issue activity, currently at a standstill before the New Year's Day holiday, is expected to touchdown in full force in '97 as attractive rates lure players back into the field, dealers said.
"There's no activity right now...everything's on hold until the new year," said one syndicate source.
"With rates at still very attractive levels, issuance is sure to pick up," he added.
Among expected issues next year are a $1.0 billion 10-year global debt offering for Italy, syndicate sources said.
State Development Bank of China is said to also be preparing a deal of its own consisting of $300 million in 10-year yankee debt, syndicate sources said.
Among upcoming junk issues, Tenet Healthcare is getting set to bring a two-part debt offering consisting of $800 million in notes due 2007 and $500 million in notes due 2007, market sources said.
The deal is expected to be underwritten by Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities.
Also, Multicanal SA, an Argentinian cable company, is expected to sell $250 million in junk bonds via a 144A private debt offering via Credit Suisse First Boston, sources said.
New zero coupon bond deals are also expected to reappear in early 1997, after having faded for several months.

Issuers include Optelcom, which is expected to issue $150 million in zeros, General Wireless which is preparing a $220 million deal and UIH Australia/Pacific Inc, which is expected to issue a $150 million zero coupon issue, dealers added.

Other junk bond issuers expected to tap the market in the new year are Systems International, Corning Clinical Labs, Bresnan Communications, ACF Industries, Syratech Corp, Pocket Communications and Premier Parks, high-yield sources said.
In 1996, straight corporate debt issuance is expected to surpass 1993's record volume for issuance according to research firm Securities Data Co.
A sharp drop in U.S. Treasury yields triggered the avalanche of debt offerings as U.S. corporations took advantage of lower financing costs, syndicate managers said.
Early estimates saw corporate debt issuance approaching $290 billion in 1996, topping 1993's record volume of $286 billion level, the firm said.
Among early December estimates $30 billion in new high-yield bonds have been issued thus far in 1996, putting junk bonds on track for their highest levels since 1993 as well.
Analysts expect the trend to continue with good high-yield supply boosted by attractive rates, demand for paper and pension fund money flowing into the sector.
Last week, AMG Data Services reported inflows into junk mutual funds at a healthy $310 million for the week, market sources said on Friday. An official at AMG Data would not comment.
Approximately $268 billion in new investment grade debt was priced in the corporate bond market this year, according to Securities Data.
